statement: The five-number summaries of the scores on the same test for two classes are shown below. $$\begin{array}{l|c|c|c|c|c} & \text{Min} & Q_1 & \text{Median} & Q_3 & \text{Max} \\ \hline \text{Class P} & 55 & 68 & 79 & 86 & 98 \\ \text{Class Q} & 50 & 61 & 70 & 79 & 94 \end{array}$$ The number of students in each class is not given. Which of the following statements must be true?

choices.text: The interquartile range of class P's scores is greater than that of class Q's scores.
choices.misconception: I compared the third quartiles, 86 and 79, and thought the class with the higher third quartile must have the larger interquartile range.

choices.text: The range of class P's scores is greater than that of class Q's scores.
choices.misconception: I compared only the maximum scores, 98 and 94, and forgot that the range also depends on the minimum scores.

choices.text: More students in class Q than in class P scored below $70$.
choices.misconception: I saw that half of class Q scored below 70 and fewer than half of class P did, and I assumed the two classes have the same number of students.

choices.text: At least half of the students in class P scored $79$ or higher.

hints: Compute each class's interquartile range and range before deciding.
Remember what the median guarantees, and notice that the class sizes are unknown.
Both interquartile ranges are $18$. The ranges are $43$ for P and $44$ for Q. Class P's median is $79$.

solutions.reliable: The interquartile ranges are $86 - 68 = 18$ and $79 - 61 = 18$, which are equal, so the first statement is false. The ranges are $98 - 55 = 43$ and $94 - 50 = 44$, so the second statement is false. Half of class Q scored below $70$ and fewer than half of class P did, but without class sizes we cannot compare the numbers of students, so the third statement need not be true. Class P's median is $79$, so at least half of class P scored $79$ or higher. That statement must be true.
